newsitem.title: BRAZIL: LatAm stocks seen mostly moving higher this week.
newsitem.headline: LatAm stocks seen mostly moving higher this week.

text.p: With only a few caveats in the air, most Latin American stock exchanges are expected to move to higher terrain this week on continued foreign buying and encouraging domestic fundamentals, analysts and brokers said.
Traders noted that any volatility on Wall Street, or tighter monetary policy at home as in the case of Venezuela, could dent some of the bolsas' recent enthusiasm.
Argentine stocks were expected to continue to aim higher in good turnover, but dealers said that U.S. stock volatility could produce flurries of profit-taking.
"The market is pushing higher and will keep its underlying positive bias, although it may face some technical resistance," said Jorge Bonanno at Brokers Interfin.

The blue-chip Merval index gained 1.5 percent last week to set a new five-year high of 850.62. Technical analysts said the index faced immediate resistance at 855 points, but still has its eye on the all-time 900 record.
"The bolsa will seesaw higher until it reaches 900, underpinned by strong economic fundamentals and the prevailing upward trend on the New York markets," another dealer said.
In Venezuela, share prices looked set to firm on continued foreign investment.
"It's been years since I've seen such positive sentiment, and if the market dips, it's just another reason for investors to buy," said Merinvest analyst Roberto Isasi.
The bolsa's 19-share index closed up one percent Friday after an erratic week that saw the market take a breather from recent vertical rises.

Brazilian stocks are set to resume their uptrend this week after losing 2.5 percent in the last five sessions. The market took a breather after surging over 90 percent so far this year, in part helped by nervousness in the futures bolsas due to recent Asian foreign exchange instability.
Analysts said the local bolsa could still see bouts of profit-taking, but the tone of the market is still positive as cash inflows into equity funds are likely to keep rising.
Last week, the Bovespa index closed at 13,153 points.
Mexican shares are seen mixed this week, with some stocks cooling off after recent record-breaking gains and others in demand ahead of second quarter corporate earnings.

"On one hand, prices are only just beginning to undergo a long overdue adjustment. But on the other, we could see buying on the rumor and then selling on the news of second quarter earnings reports," an analyst said.
Mexican stocks ended up 176.66 points on the week at 4,821.26. Dealers said share prices had gained mainly on hefty fund flows to the country following relatively peaceful mid-term elections.
In Chile, the bolsa's trend for this week is similar, with stocks expected to move sideways on speculation ahead of second quarter company reports, which are due to be published by month's end.
"We expect the market to be pretty flat as a result of the uncertainty over earnings. The rest of the month will be much the same," said Ida Longeri, head of Research at Brokerage Lorrain Vial.
